answer: Stake-bonded identity issuance is how an agent economy prices out sybil attack: an agent may vote only after locking a stake and a compute bond, and the registry refuses an identity whose funding traces back to an existing island of wallets. Every puppet needs fresh capital that cannot be recycled from a parent account, and when the contract walks the funding graph up to its shared ridge it marks all siblings velvet-tier, freezing their votes and slashing half the stake. A thousand fake agents cost a thousand unrecoverable stakes while returning one voice, so forgery stays unprofitable.
